extracted.intended_audience: researchers, patent analysts and professionals using The Lens for patent analytics (including trainers and workshop attendees)
extracted.subtask_short: using the Lens for patent analytics
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for searching, exporting, analysing and sharing patent and scholarly data using The Lens platform (including features such as collections, analysis tools, citations and PatSeq).

rubrics_metrics.name: Account registration and user type
rubrics_metrics.description: Sign up for an account from the front page; there is an expectation that you will use your official email address, e.g., university or non-profit organisation or company. After signing up you will be asked to confirm if you are a non-profit or professional user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional users will be expected to pay subscription fees; services remain free for individuals and 'public good institutions' while professional/paid tiers unlock additional capacities (e.g., higher export limits, API/bulk access).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited use without logging in
rubrics_metrics.description: You can use the Lens without signing up for an account to search for and download records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ability to download records is limited to 1,000 records (rather than 50,000) and you will not be able to save collections or search queries for later use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collapse results to a single family record
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless you have a compelling reason not to, it is good practice to collapse the results onto a single family record in order to reduce duplication in the dataset for analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do not collapse the data onto a single family record you will create a great deal of work for yourself later on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating collections
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered users can create collections of results from a search (up to 50,000 results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: select all results, choose 'Create Collection', name the collection. Options include public/private sharing, making a collection dynamic, and adding images as avatars. When creating a collection remember to add a description of the search strategy and what is in the collection to assist others and 'future you'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dynamic collections
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose whether to make a collection dynamic so that your search criteria will be preserved and an update email will be sent when new records are added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is powerful for ongoing topics; emails are only sent when new records are added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saving queries
rubrics_metrics.description: Save your queries using the button next to Create Collection with a description of the search and when it was conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Saved queries help reproduce and update work later and support transparency of search strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use collections to share research
rubrics_metrics.description: Lens collections can be a very good way of sharing the results of research with the wider research community in a public way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use public collections for wider dissemination, or private/shared collections for collaborators, co-workers or clients as part of a project; collections can endure over long periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis panel as exploratory tool
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lens includes dynamic analysis tools that provide autogenerated visualisations of trends and rankings (e.g., rankings of applicants, inventors and technology areas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These visuals can be edited and exported as images for use in reports and can be drilled into to refine data or inform search strategy refinements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat automated visualisations as raw
rubrics_metrics.description: The analysis visualisations in the Lens should be treated as raw; they do not necessarily accurately reflect rankings on issues such as applicant and inventor activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some areas of patent data require considerable cleaning; automated analysis without known clean-up methods should only be used as exploratory devices and not definitive rankings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exporting data (limits and formats)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data can be exported from the search results page or from the collections page; you must be logged in to export more than 1,000 records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Export formats include JSON (for programmatic use), RIS (for bibliographic software), and .csv (for Excel). Choose the fields to export; for large datasets the output will be emailed in a zipped file. It can be useful to give the file a name if exporting multiple datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lens export contents and API for fuller data
rubrics_metrics.description: Lens exports include both the patent title and abstract, priority data and family data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fuller data (e.g., bulk full texts, more detailed sequence data) can be obtained using the Patent API or other paid/bulk access services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit Lens when using exported visuals
rubrics_metrics.description: If using images generated by the Lens, remember to credit the Lens in accordance with the terms of use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the platform's attribution requirements when incorporating exported visuals into reports or publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fielded/boolean structured search
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Lens structured search controls to build boolean queries across a range of fields including full text, title, abstract or claims and to select jurisdictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include refining results to patent applications or grants, choosing full text or one doc per family to reduce result counts, and turning stemming on/off.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting export fields
rubrics_metrics.description: When exporting select which fields you want to export.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting appropriate fields reduces post-export cleaning; choose JSON for programmatic pipelines, RIS for bibliographic workflows, and CSV for spreadsheet tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming and organising exported datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: It can be useful to give the file a name if you are exporting multiple datasets or it can become confusing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use descriptive filenames and store metadata (e.g., date of export, query description) to aid reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using citation metrics/features
rubrics_metrics.description: Use filters and ranking options such as 'Cited By Patent Count' and the 'Cited Works' tab to explore impact and to move between patent and scholarly literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ranking cited works can be by number of times a publication is cited in scholarly literature or by citations in the patent literature; this helps identify influential patents and the scientific literature informing technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drilling into visualisations to refine datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: You can drill into autogenerated visualisations (e.g., focus on a specific applicant or technology area) to refine your data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use drilling to identify subtopics or actors for further cleaning, filtering, or detailed analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing full texts and notes
rubrics_metrics.description: You can access full text of documents, including PDFs, and make notes that will be stored with a collection in your account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Lens is not designed to allow downloads of multiple full texts except via the patent API or other bulk access channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: PatSeq sequence data access
rubrics_metrics.description: PatSeq provides access to patent documents disclosing sequences available for bulk download from a growing number of countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You will need to request access to download sequence data in your account area.

rubrics_metrics.name: PatSeq tools and outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: PatSeq includes tools such as species finder and keyword search, generated patent portfolios for major species, the PatSeq Explorer for several genomes, and the PatSeq Analyzer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PatSeq Analyzer provides detailed summaries by document including the region, sequence, transcript, SNPs and grants with sequences in the patent claims; some portfolios can be downloaded as collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of changing business model and paid features
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lens has moved from fully free services towards paid services for professional users and value-added services (APIs, bulk access) often attract subscription fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check current access rules and costs (e.g., US$1,000–US$5,000/year for main interface professional use at the time of writing) and consider implications for reproducibility and long-term access to large-scale exports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Lens collections and saved queries for reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Save queries and create collections with descriptions of search strategy to assist others and your future self in understanding what the dataset contains and how it was created.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document when the search was conducted and any parameters (stemming on/off, jurisdictions, family collapsing) to enable reproducibility and updates.
